title:
Patient Report
Redesign
subtitle: From a blank page into a structured, shareable communication tool.

slides.title:
Patient Report
Redesign
slides.description: Doctors were using the patient report — the tool just couldn't keep up. I had to add everything they needed without making it harder to use.
slides.presenterNotes: אז הקייס הזה הוא על ה־Patient Report — הכלי שבו רופאי שיניים מתקשרים עם המטופלים אחרי הסריקה. זה חלק מה־Align Oral Health Suite, החבילה הקלינית של אליין. עיצבתי אותו מחדש כדי שיתמוך בכל מה שרופאים באמת היו צריכים — בלי לסבך את העבודה. עבדתי על זה ב־2025 עם PM, הנדסה, וצוות מחקר קליני.

slides.label: Context
slides.title: Where the patient report lives in the workflow
slides.content: Part of the Align Oral Health Suite — the moment after the scan, when clinical findings turn into something the patient takes home.
issues: Generated chair-side — patient still in the room
Pulls images from the iTero snapshot tool
Read by the patient at home, without the doctor
Often the only artifact they keep from the visit
slides.highlight: If the patient can't read it, the clinical work doesn't land.

image.caption: The report sits between the scan and the patient's decision

slides.presenterNotes: ה־Patient Report חי בתוך ה־Align Oral Health Suite — אחרי הסריקה, הרופא משתף את הדוח עם המטופל דרך QR code ישר בחדר. הנקודה — המטופל קורא את זה בבית בלי הסבר. אם הוא לא מבין, העבודה הקלינית לא מגיעה ליעדה.

slides.label: The Problem
slides.title: A blank page after every appointment
slides.content: Doctors were using the report — the ceiling was the problem, not adoption.
issues: Sidebar locked doctor info into 25% of the screen
No templates — every report started blank
No modular blocks — no cost breakdown, before/after, or treatment plan
PDF output not readable by patients
slides.highlight: The report was built to be filled in — not to be useful.

image.caption: Old UI — sidebar-locked editing, blank content area, QR-only sharing

slides.presenterNotes: הבעיה הייתה שאנשים השתמשו ב־report — הם פשוט נתקלו בתקרה. הסיידבר תפס רבע מהמסך, כל דוח התחיל מדף ריק, לא היה איך להוסיף עלות או before/after, וה־PDF שיצא בסוף היה לא קריא למטופל. בעצם הכלי נבנה למלא — לא להיות שימושי.

slides.label: Who Uses It
slides.title: Four specialties, four different reports
description: Four specialties, four reporting jobs. One report had to handle all of them — without becoming the lowest common denominator.

issues.title: General dentists
issues.description: High volume, fast appointments — need a clean recap they can finish before the next patient.

issues.title: Restorative specialists
issues.description: Complex cases — need before/after, cost breakdowns, and visual context to justify treatment.

issues.title: Orthodontists
issues.description: Long-term treatment — need progress tracking and the ability to mark specific teeth.

issues.title: Implantologists
issues.description: High-stakes decisions — need detailed reports the patient can review before committing.

slides.presenterNotes: הדוח לא משמש קבוצה אחת של רופאים — הוא משמש ארבע התמחויות שונות, וכל אחת צריכה דוח שמדבר בשפה אחרת. רופא כללי צריך משהו מהיר וקצר, מומחה שיקום צריך לראות לפני־אחרי ועלויות, אורתודנט צריך מעקב לאורך זמן, ואימפלנטולוג צריך לבסס החלטה כבדה. השאלה הייתה — איך אני בונה דוח אחד שמשרת את כולם בלי להפוך לכזה שלא משרת אף אחד.

slides.label: User Research
slides.title: What doctors told me
slides.content:
I interviewed doctors across four specialties. 
They weren't complaining about the report existing — they were working around everything it couldn't do.

quotes.text: Every report takes me 10 minutes from scratch. I'm doing it after the patient leaves.
quotes.author: Dr. A, General Practice

quotes.text: Patients ask me to explain things the report doesn't show.
quotes.author: Dr. B, Restorative

quotes.text: I have no way to circle what I'm talking about on the image.
quotes.author: Dr. C, Orthodontics

quotes.text: Every report looks different — there's no standard starting point.
quotes.author: Dr. D, Implantology

slides.presenterNotes: ראיינתי רופאים מכל ארבעת ההתמחויות. המעניין היה שהם לא התלוננו שהדוח קיים — הם דווקא רצו להשתמש בו. הם פשוט עקפו את כל מה שהוא לא יכל לעשות, או נאלצו להשלים את הדוח אחרי שהמטופל יצא מהחדר.

slides.label: Pain Points
slides.title: Three pain points, three design moves
description: Three problems, three answers. The case study from here on is how I built each one.

issues.title: Reports take too long
issues.description: No starting point, no structure. Fix: procedure templates.

issues.title: Reports describe — they don't show
issues.description: Long text next to images that should do the talking. Fix: in-image annotation and tooth tagging.

issues.title: No standard structure
issues.description: Every doctor invents their own format. Fix: procedure-based templates with consistent ordering.

slides.presenterNotes: שלוש נקודות כאב, שלוש תשובות עיצוביות. הדוח לוקח יותר מדי זמן — Templates. הדוח מתאר ולא מראה — Annotation. אין מבנה אחיד — procedure-based templates עם סדר עקבי. כל החלטה אחרי זה היא תשובה לאחת מהשלוש.

slides.label: Design Goals
slides.title: What I set out to fix

goals.title: Give the canvas back
goals.description: Move metadata and actions to the header — full screen for editing.

goals.title: Give doctors a starting point
goals.description: Procedure templates so reports start structured, not blank.

goals.title: Make findings visual
goals.description: Annotation and tooth tagging — show, don't describe.

kpis: Time to create a complete report
slides.description:
Each goal answers the same question: how do I add more without overwhelming the doctor? 
Everything here came from doctors — nothing assumed.
slides.presenterNotes: ארבע מטרות עיצוב, וכל אחת צמודה ל־KPI שאני יכול למדוד. השאלה שהובילה אותי — איך אני מוסיף הרבה יותר תוכן ופונקציונליות, בלי שהרופא ירגיש שהכלי הפך מסובך יותר. כל מטרה כאן הגיעה ממה שרופאים אמרו לי בראיונות, לא מהנחות שלי.

slides.label: Constraints
slides.title: What I couldn't change
description:
Every design decision had to fit inside three fixed boundaries. 
Naming them upfront kept the scope honest — and made the work that did ship realistic.

issues.title: The PDF engine couldn't be replaced
issues.description: Output had to work with the existing renderer — every design decision had to respect what the engine could produce.

issues.title: Annotation had to ship without ML
issues.description: No AI-assisted findings in v1 — the annotation tools had to give doctors full manual control.

issues.title: Sharing flow had to stay the same
issues.description: Privacy and consent rules were locked. I could reorder and reframe the steps, but not change what they did — same steps, better surface.

slides.presenterNotes: שלוש מגבלות שלא יכולתי לעקוף. מנוע ה־PDF הקיים נשאר, אז כל עיצוב היה צריך לעבוד עם מה שהוא יודע לרנדר. ML היה outside scope לגרסה הראשונה, אז annotation היה חייב להיות ידני. ובשיתוף — בגלל פרטיות ו־consent, אותם שלבים שהיו קודם היו חייבים להישאר. מה שיכלתי לעשות זה לארגן אותם מחדש ולהציג אותם טוב יותר, אבל לא לשנות מה הם עושים. שמתי את זה על השולחן בהתחלה כדי שה־scope יישאר ישים.

slides.label: Features
slides.title: Four features, one workflow
description: The redesign wasn't one feature — it was a coordinated rebuild from the canvas down. Each piece below was designed and tested to fit alongside the others, not as a standalone addition.

issues.title: Templates
issues.description: Five procedure-based starting points so reports begin structured, not blank — General Scan, Implant, Crown Prep, Follow-up, Custom.

issues.title: Modular blocks
issues.description: Eight composable content blocks doctors can add, reorder, or remove — color-coded by function so they read at a glance.

issues.title: Annotation & tooth chart
issues.description: Pen, text, color, and FDI tooth tagging — findings get marked on the image instead of explained around it.

issues.title: Sharing modal
issues.description: Same sharing flow, rebuilt as one continuous modal — clearer steps, better hierarchy, sharing now part of the report instead of three buttons after it.

slides.presenterNotes: זה לא היה פיצ'ר אחד — זה היה ארבעה פיצ'רים שעובדים יחד כמערכת. Templates נותנים לרופא נקודת התחלה. Modular blocks נותנים לו שליטה. Annotation מאפשרת לסמן ממצאים על התמונה. ו־Sharing — אותו flow קיים, אבל עוצב מחדש כ־modal רציף עם היררכיה ברורה יותר. כל אחד עוצב להיות חלק מהשני, לא כפיצ'ר נפרד.

slides.label: Structure
slides.title: Four features, one structure
slides.content: With the features named, I mapped how they live inside one workflow — scan finishes, template loads, doctor edits and annotates, patient receives the report. Every feature had to fit into that flow without becoming its own detour.
slides.highlight: The flow holds the features together.

image.caption: Report workflow map — scan → template → edit → share → patient view

slides.presenterNotes: אחרי שהיו לי ארבעת הפיצ'רים, מיפיתי איך הם מתחברים ל־flow אחד רציף. הסריקה נגמרת, ה־template נטען, הרופא עורך ומסמן, המטופל מקבל את הדוח. הזרימה היא מה שמחזיק את הפיצ'רים ביחד — בלי המבנה הזה, כל פיצ'ר יכל להפוך לעצירה נפרדת.

slides.label: Low-Fidelity Wireframes
slides.title: Two structures, sketched fast
slides.dir1Desc: Sidebar does the editing. All controls — text, tooth tagging, notes — live in the panel. The canvas only shows what the sidebar changes.
slides.dir2Desc: Canvas does the editing. The sidebar becomes a block library — a place to add new content, not edit existing content. Everything that changes the report happens on the report.
slides.description: Before polish, I sketched both directions as wireframes — the cheapest way to ask the structural question without committing to either. Both got built. Both got tested.
slides.presenterNotes: לפני שעיצבתי ב־full fidelity, סקיצתי שני מבנים. בראשון — הסיידבר עושה את כל העבודה. כל עריכה — טקסט, תיוג שיניים, הערות — קורה בפאנל, והקנבס רק מציג את התוצאה. בשני — הקנבס עושה את כל העבודה. הסיידבר הופך לספריית בלוקים — מקום להוסיף תוכן חדש, לא לערוך תוכן קיים. שתי גישות שונות לאותה שאלה — איפה הרופא צריך לעבוד.

slides.label: Ideation
slides.title: The same two directions — at full fidelity
slides.dir1Desc: Edit from the sidebar. Controls sit in a side panel, the canvas is just a preview — you change one place and check another.
slides.dir2Desc: Edit on the content. Annotate, tag teeth, title and note each image right where it sits. The control lives on the thing it changes.
slides.description: After wireframe testing pointed to in-place editing, I built both directions out at full fidelity — same content, polished UI — and tested again. Every doctor preferred editing in place: less context switching, faster to finish.
slides.presenterNotes: אחרי שה־wireframes הצביעו על עריכה ישירה, בניתי את שני הכיוונים ב־full fidelity ובדקתי שוב. אותו תוכן, UI מלוטש, ועם רופאים אמיתיים. כל רופא שבדק העדיף לערוך ישירות על התוכן — פחות מעבר בין אזורים, יותר מהיר. הבדיקה הראתה שגם אם הסיידבר נראה מוכר, הוא בפועל יוצר יותר חיכוך.

slides.label: Block Composition
slides.title: Which blocks belong in which template
slides.content: With the editing model decided, I mapped each block to the templates that needed it — based on what each procedure has to communicate.
slides.issuesTitle: Five templates, mapped to the blocks each one needs
issues: General — general-purpose recap (Image + Notes)
Implant — surgical planning with cost and follow-up details
Crown — visual case first, with before/after and cost
Follow-up — progress tracking with comparison and next steps
From scratch — blank, just an image to start

image.caption: Template composition matrix — which blocks pre-load for which template

slides.presenterNotes: מיפיתי איזה בלוק שייך לאיזה תבנית. כל תא במטריצה הוא החלטה. Implant מתחיל עם Cost Summary כי המטופל צריך לקבל החלטה כלכלית. Crown מתחיל עם Before/After כי המקרה נמכר ויזואלית. כל תבנית מבטאת דעה קלינית של איך הפרוצדורה צריכה להיות מוצגת.

slides.label: Block Categories
slides.title: Colors that doctors can scan, not memorise
slides.content: Once the blocks were assigned to templates, each block got a color tied to what it does. The color isn't decoration — it tells the doctor what kind of content they're looking at without reading the label.
issues: Visual (blue) — Image, Image Gallery
Comparison (coral) — Before / After
Outcome (green) — Summary, Cost
Next step (teal) — Next Appointment
Free-form (purple) — Notes
Clinical instructions (pink) — Prescription, Patient Instructions

image.caption: Six color families — one per functional category

slides.presenterNotes: כל בלוק קיבל צבע שמייצג את התפקיד שלו. כחול לויזואלי כי זה מה שהמטופל מסתכל עליו. קורל להשוואה כי זה מסמן שינוי לאורך זמן. ירוק לתוצאה — Summary ו־Cost — מה שסוגר את הביקור. טורקיז לצעד הבא — Next Appointment — מה שפותח את הביקור הבא. סגול ל־Notes כי זה החופש של הרופא לכתוב בשפה שלו. ורוד להוראות קליניות — Prescription ו־Patient Instructions — מה שהמטופל לוקח הביתה. רופאים סורקים דוחות מהר בין מטופלים, והקטגוריות נותנות להם למצוא את הבלוק הנכון במבט אחד. הצבע הוא חיזוק — לכל בלוק יש גם אייקון וגם שם.

slides.label: Templates & Sections
slides.title: A structured starting point
slides.content: With the blocks defined and colored, the templates became a question of packaging — which blocks ship together for which procedure. The structure was ready before the doctor opened a report.
issues: Five templates — General Scan, Implant, Crown Prep, Follow-up, Custom
Pre-loaded with sections for that procedure
Modular blocks composed from the library
Drag to reorder, duplicate, or delete
slides.highlight: Templates give a running start. Blocks give control.
slides.presenterNotes: וזאת התוצאה — חמש תבניות, כל אחת עם המבנה הקליני שלה. הרופא בוחר את הפרוצדורה והדוח מוכן עוד לפני שהוא פותח אותו. הוא יכול להוסיף, להזיז, או למחוק בלוקים — אבל הוא לא מתחיל מדף ריק. תבניות נותנות התחלה רצה, בלוקים נותנים שליטה.

slides.label: The Next Question
slides.question: Once the report had a shape — how do you make the findings inside it actually communicate?
slides.support: Templates gave doctors structure. Blocks gave them control. But findings were still text next to images that should have been doing the talking. Editing the report wasn't enough — the findings themselves needed a way to be shown.
slides.presenterNotes: ברגע שהדוח קיבל צורה, השאלה הבאה הייתה — איך הממצאים בתוכו באמת מתקשרים. עד לפה בניתי לרופא מבנה ושליטה. אבל הממצאים עצמם עדיין היו טקסט ליד תמונות שיכלו להראות הכל. צריך לעבור משלב העריכה לשלב התקשורת.

slides.label: Looking Outward
slides.title: How other tools let users mark up an image
slides.content: I looked at how other software handles image markup. The pattern was consistent — a small set of tools on the canvas, with the artifact interactive underneath.
slides.issuesTitle: What the design space agreed on
issues: A small, fixed set of tools — pen, text, shapes, color
Tools on the canvas, not in a side panel
Artifact stays interactive — annotation is a layer on top
Marks save with the file
slides.highlight: Annotation is a solved pattern. The work was adapting it — not reinventing it.
slides.presenterNotes: במקום להמציא משהו חדש, הסתכלתי איך תוכנות אחרות פותרות את אותה בעיה של סימון על תמונה. הדפוס היה זהה בכולן — סט קטן וקבוע של כלים על הקנבס, התמונה נשארת אינטראקטיבית, וכל הסימונים נשמרים עם הקובץ. annotation הוא דפוס פתור. העבודה שלי הייתה ליישם אותו, לא להמציא מחדש.

slides.label: Annotation & Tooth Chart
slides.title: From plain scans to annotated findings
slides.content: Doctors were writing long descriptions next to images patients couldn't read. I added two tools so findings get marked on the image — not explained around it.
issues: Pen, text, color — annotate at full size
Tooth chart — click to tag affected teeth, shown as markers
Patients see which teeth are affected
slides.highlight: Show, don't describe — the principle behind both.
slides.presenterNotes: אז ככה זה נראה בסוף. שני כלים — annotation על התמונה עצמה עם עט, טקסט וצבעים, וגם tooth chart שבה הרופא מסמן את השיניים המעורבות. המטופל רואה בדיוק על איזו שן מדובר ומה הממצא. הרעיון פשוט — להראות, לא לתאר. זה הקשר שהיה חסר בין הטקסט לתמונה.

slides.label: Share & Export
slides.title: Same flow, rebuilt as one modal
slides.beforeDescription: Three sidebar buttons — Download PDF, WeChat, QR code. Each one isolated, no shared surface.
slides.afterDescription: Same three options, restructured as one modal — clear title, options grouped, QR code visible by default with a refresh action.
slides.description: Three isolated buttons became one structured modal — delivery as part of the report, not a step after it.
slides.presenterNotes: השיתוף לפני ואחרי. לפני — שלושה כפתורים בודדים בסיידבר, כל אחד מבודד, בלי הקשר משותף. אחרי — אותן שלוש אפשרויות, אבל מאורגנות כ־modal אחד עם כותרת ברורה, אפשרויות מקובצות, וה־QR code גלוי כברירת מחדל. אותו flow, אותן יכולות — פשוט סופית מאורגן. זה היה הקונסטריינט — לא יכלתי לשנות את ה־flow בגלל פרטיות ו־consent, אבל יכלתי לעצב מחדש איך הוא מוצג.

slides.label: Doctor Feedback
slides.quote: The templates actually match what I do, and everything I need is right there in front of me.
slides.author: Dr. N. Haddad
slides.context: Feedback collected during the iTero early access program, before full rollout.
slides.presenterNotes: הציטוט הזה הגיע מ־early access program של iTero, עוד לפני ההשקה המלאה. הוא תופס בדיוק את מה שניסיתי לעשות — תבניות שמתאימות לעבודה האמיתית של הרופא, וכל מה שהוא צריך גלוי במקום אחד. זה האישור שהמערכת עובדת לא רק ב־Figma אלא בחדר טיפולים.

slides.label: Outcomes
slides.title: Early-access results

outcomes.title: Report creation
outcomes.description: Templates removed the blank-page barrier — doctors started from structure, not nothing.

outcomes.title: Clinical communication
outcomes.description: Findings marked on the image — clearer for patients, faster for the doctor.

outcomes.title: Completion rate
outcomes.description: Reports came back more complete — and more detailed than the old tool allowed.

outcomes.title: Reach per report
outcomes.description: Reports reached patients on the channel they actually check — email, WhatsApp, WeChat, or QR.

slides.presenterNotes: התוצאות מ־early access. ארבע נקודות מאומתות איכותית — יצירת דוח מהירה יותר, תקשורת קלינית ברורה יותר, יותר השלמת דוחות, ויותר מטופלים מקבלים את הדוח בערוץ הנכון. חשוב לציין — אלה איתותים מוקדמים, לא מדדים סופיים. המספרים הכמותיים נמצאים במעקב אחרי ההשקה המלאה.

slides.label: Reflection
slides.title: What I'd do differently
whatWorked: Using AI to generate concept directions early — explored more structural options in less time.
The interactive prototype made annotation testable — doctors marked up images and felt how it behaved, not just looked at static frames.
Modular blocks — the right balance between freedom and consistency.
Color-coding blocks by category — doctors scanned reports without reading every label.
whatFailed: Designing for four specialties at once — every block had to work for a general dentist's recap and an implantologist's plan, without becoming the lowest common denominator.
Working inside the existing sharing flow — privacy and consent were locked, so the modal had to feel new while keeping every step patients knew.
Annotation couldn't be tested in static frames — required building it in the prototype and iterating on how marking actually felt.
whatYoudDoDifferently: Pull engineering into sharing constraints earlier — privacy edge cases shaped the modal.
Add AI-assisted field completion — drafting notes and procedure suggestions as the doctor works.
Let doctors create their own templates — five presets were a starting point, not a ceiling.
slides.whatYouLearned: Each feature had to earn its place in the workflow.
slides.whatYouCouldntMeasure: Long-term adoption and how doctors customize templates — needs 6+ months of field data.
slides.presenterNotes: מה עבד — AI לקונספטים בשלבים מוקדמים, prototype אינטראקטיבי שאיפשר לבדוק annotation באמת, modular blocks, וצבעי קטגוריות. האתגרים — לעצב לארבע התמחויות בלי להפוך ל־lowest common denominator, לעבוד בתוך flow שיתוף נעול, ולמצוא איך לבדוק annotation שלא ניתן לבדיקה ב־frames סטטיים. הצעדים הבאים — annotation ב־prototype מהיום הראשון, הנדסה מוקדם יותר ל־edge cases של privacy, AI שיכתוב הערות אוטומטית, ו־templates שרופאים יוצרים בעצמם.

slides.title: Thank You
slides.subtitle: I fix the defaults professionals shouldn't have to manage.
slides.presenterNotes: אז סיכום — ניסיתי לעצב כלי שעוזר לרופאים להעביר את מה שהם רואים למטופלים בצורה שהם באמת יכולים להבין. החזון שלי — אני מתקן את ברירות המחדל שאנשי מקצוע לא צריכים להתעסק איתן. תודה.

article.title: Patient Report Redesign
article.lede: Rebuilding the post-scan patient report — from a blank page doctors filled by hand into a templated, annotated document patients can actually read.

items.label: Problem
items.text: Every report started as a blank page in a 25%-wide sidebar. Doctors spent ~10 minutes assembling each one — usually after the patient had left — and findings ended up as text beside images that should have been doing the talking.

items.label: Solution
items.text: Editing moved onto the canvas, with the sidebar rebuilt as a block library. Eight modular blocks compose into five procedure templates, and findings get marked directly on the scan with annotation and FDI tooth tagging.

items.label: Impact
items.text: Shipped to the iTero early access program across four specialties — faster to create, more complete on return, and readable by the patient at home without the doctor there to explain it.

blocks.text: The only thing the patient takes home

Part of the Align Oral Health Suite. The report is generated chair-side, while the patient is still in the room, pulling images from the iTero scan. It's read later — at home, alone, without the doctor there to explain it. Four specialties use it: **general practice, restorative, orthodontics, implantology** — each needing the report to do a different job.

media.caption: The report sits between the scan and the patient's decision

blocks.text: If the patient can't read it, the clinical work doesn't land.
A blank page after every appointment
**Doctors were using the report — the ceiling was the problem, not adoption.** They weren't asking for it to exist. They were working around everything it couldn't do.

blocks.title: Where it failed
items: **Every report started from nothing** — no structure, no starting point. Around ten minutes to assemble one, usually after the patient had already left the room.
**Findings were described, not shown** — paragraphs of text sitting beside images that could have carried the same information instantly, with no way to mark a specific tooth or area.
**The canvas was locked to 25%** — doctor and patient details took a fixed sidebar, leaving a fraction of the screen for the content that actually matters.
**No modular content** — no cost breakdown, no before/after, no treatment plan. What the report could say was capped by what the form allowed.
**Every doctor invented their own format** — nothing was consistent between two reports, let alone between two specialties.
**The PDF wasn't written for patients** — the artifact they took home was the one part nobody had designed for its actual reader.

media.caption: Old UI — sidebar locked to 25%, canvas starts blank, sharing as three isolated buttons

blocks.text: Quote text

quotes.text: Every report takes me 10 minutes from scratch. I'm doing it after the patient leaves.
quotes.author: General Practice

quotes.text: I have no way to circle what I'm talking about on the image.
quotes.author: Orthodontics

blocks.text: What I set out to fix

These aren't separate complaints. They're one condition: the report could only hold what a doctor typed into it, so structure, clarity and consistency all had to come from the doctor's own effort, on every single visit. The goals below move that work onto the product.

items.title: Give the canvas back
items.text: Move metadata and actions to the header — full screen for editing.

items.title: Give doctors a starting point
items.text: Procedure templates so reports start structured, not blank.

items.title: Make findings visual
items.text: Annotation and tooth tagging — show, don't describe.

blocks.title: How we'd know it worked
items: Time to create a complete report
Patient engagement with the shared report

blocks.text: Where each piece meets the appointment

Named separately, these read like additions to a tool. In practice they all interrupt the same twenty minutes of a real visit. So before designing any of them I mapped them onto that visit: the scan finishes, a template loads, the doctor edits and annotates while the patient is still in the chair, the patient opens the report later at home. Anything that pulled the doctor out of that line was the wrong answer, however well it worked on its own.

media.caption: Report workflow map — scan → template → edit → share → patient view

blocks.text: Two editing models for one report

Templates, blocks and annotation all land on the same screen, and every one of them behaves differently depending on a single question: does the doctor work **on** the report, or beside it? That had to be answered before any of the pieces could be designed. I sketched two directions as wireframes first, then built both at full fidelity and tested them with doctors.
Editing from the sidebar
All controls — text, tooth tagging, notes — live in the side panel. The canvas only shows what the sidebar changes.

items: **Familiar and cheap to build** — it's how the existing tool already worked, so nothing had to be relearned or rebuilt from zero.
**The canvas stays clean** — a true preview of the PDF, with no editing chrome sitting on top of a document that also has to print.
**But you change one place and check another.** Every edit is a round trip between panel and canvas, and the cost compounds across a report with eight blocks.
**And it doesn't scale to annotation.** Marking a specific tooth on a specific image from a side panel means selecting the target first, then the tool — two steps for what should be one.

blocks.text: Editing on the content
Every control sits on the block it changes. The sidebar becomes a block library — a place to add new content, not to edit existing content.

items: **No context switching** — annotate, tag teeth, title and note each image right where it sits.
**One surface serves both jobs** — the same canvas is the editor and the preview, so what the doctor builds is what the patient receives.
**But controls on the canvas risk clutter** — a document that has to render cleanly to PDF can't carry visible editing chrome.
**And more of the interface becomes discoverable rather than listed** — nothing announces what's editable until you interact with it.

media.caption: Wireframe — canvas edits, sidebar becomes a block library

blocks.text: We chose editing on the content, based on explicit tradeoffs. Direct manipulation was critical for this use case — the control has to live on the thing it changes. But the two concerns were real, and we resolved them before committing.
Five templates, eight blocks — structure without a lowest common denominator

With the editing model settled, the question became what the doctor is editing. A general dentist's recap and an implantologist's surgical plan are not the same document — a fixed format would fail one of them, and an empty canvas was the thing we were replacing.

The resolution was composition. **Eight modular blocks** — image, gallery, before/after, summary, cost, next appointment, notes, instructions — pre-loaded into **five procedure templates**, then reorderable, duplicable, removable. Each block carries a colour tied to its function, so doctors read a report's structure without reading a single label.

media.caption: Which blocks pre-load for which template

blocks.text: Five moments in a real report
Each clip follows one part of the flow, in the order a doctor meets it — from the shape a report starts with to the moment it reaches the patient.

media.caption: **Templates & structure** — how a report gets its shape, and how it stays editable afterwards. Each of the four templates is applied in turn and scrolled through, then new blocks are inserted between existing ones.

**Adding content blocks** — how clinical detail gets added part-way through a report, not just appended at the end. Notes, a Summary and a Prescription are inserted between existing blocks and filled in, including a second medication.

**Images & before / after** — how clinical photography gets into a report, and how change over time is shown. An image block is filled from the photo gallery with title, tooth selection and notes, then a Before / After comparison is added and captioned.

**Annotation & tooth chart** — how a finding gets marked on the scan itself instead of described next to it. An image opens at full size for pen, text and colour, then the affected teeth are tagged on the FDI chart and the marks carry back into the report.

**Signing & sharing** — how a finished report is signed off and reaches the patient. The doctor's signature is drawn by hand on the pad, then Share opens and walks the PDF, WeChat and QR-code options.

blocks.text: Early-access results

Shipped to the iTero early access program. This ran pre-instrumentation, so the results below are qualitative, gathered from doctors across four specialties — measured against the goals set at the start.

items.title: Faster report creation
items.text: Templates removed the blank-page barrier — doctors started from structure, not nothing.

items.title: Clearer communication
items.text: Findings marked on the image — clearer for patients, faster for the doctor.

items.title: More complete reports
items.text: Reports came back fuller — and more detailed than the old tool allowed.

blocks.text: What I'd do differently

I'd pull engineering into the sharing constraints earlier — privacy edge cases shaped that modal more than any design decision did, and I found them late. And five templates were a starting point, not a ceiling: the next version should let doctors build their own.
